command:
set -eo pipefail
cd /tmp
df -m /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print "tmpfs_total_mb "$2}'
( MAX=0; MEM=0; while :; do U=$(df -m /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print $3}')
    [ "$U" -gt "$MAX" ] && { MAX=$U; echo "$MAX" > /tmp/.peak; }
    M=$(awk '/MemTotal/{t=$2} /MemAvailable/{a=$2} END{printf "%.0f", (t-a)/1024}' /proc/meminfo)
    [ "$M" -gt "$MEM" ] && { MEM=$M; echo "$MEM" > /tmp/.mem; }
    sleep 5; done ) & SAMPLER=$!

# The date in the index name is a durable id, not a byte guarantee -- publish the hash so
# anyone can check they got the same index. Printed, not asserted, on this first run.
DBSHA=$(sha256sum k2_standard_08gb_20250402.tar.gz | cut -d" " -f1)

echo "== unpack the standard-8 index (5.5 GiB gz -> ~8 GB of k2d) =="
mkdir -p db
tar -xzf k2_standard_08gb_20250402.tar.gz -C db
# Never rm the staged tar.gz: sticky /tmp, stage-in ran as the instance user, EPERM is not
# suppressed by `rm -f` and would kill the task under set -e. Budget for holding both copies.
test -s db/hash.k2d
HASHMB=$(( $(stat -c%s db/hash.k2d) / 1048576 ))

echo "== classify the complete SRR062634 run against standard-8 =="
# --output /dev/null: the per-read assignments for 24M pairs are gigabytes nobody reads here,
# and tmpfs is already holding the index twice. The report carries the totals.
T0=$(date +%s)
kraken2 --db db --paired --threads 8 --report out.report --output /dev/null \
  SRR062634_1.filt.fastq.gz SRR062634_2.filt.fastq.gz 2> kraken2.log
T1=$(date +%s); WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))
kill "$SAMPLER" 2>/dev/null || true
PEAK=$(cat /tmp/.peak 2>/dev/null || echo 0); RSS=$(cat /tmp/.mem 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
cat kraken2.log

# kraken2 logs "N sequences (M Mbp) processed", then classified/unclassified counts. With
# --paired a PAIR is one sequence, so N is the per-mate read count seqkit asserts.
PROC=$(awk '/sequences .*processed/{print $1; exit}' kraken2.log)
CLASS=$(awk '/sequences classified/{print $1; exit}' kraken2.log)
UNCL=$(awk '/sequences unclassified/{print $1; exit}' kraken2.log)
SUM=$(awk -v a="$CLASS" -v b="$UNCL" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", a+b}')
PCT=$(awk -v c="$CLASS" -v p="$PROC" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", 100*c/p}')
# out.report columns: pct, clade_reads, taxon_reads, rank, taxid, name
HUMAN=$(awk -F'\t' '$5==9606{gsub(/^ +/,"",$6); printf "%d", $2; exit}' out.report)
HUMANPCT=$(awk -v h="$HUMAN" -v p="$PROC" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", 100*h/p}')
# `| head -3` would SIGPIPE sort under `pipefail` (exit 141) -- awk reads to EOF instead.
TOPS=$(awk -F'\t' '$4=="S"{gsub(/^ +/,"",$6); print $2"\t"$5"\t"$6}' out.report | sort -k1,1nr | awk 'NR<=3')
TOPTAX=$(printf '%s' "$TOPS" | awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{print $2}')
# 1000 Genomes samples are EBV-transformed lymphoblastoid cell lines, so the virus used to
# immortalise the line is expected to appear. Asserted as "present", not as an exact count:
# the claim worth making is that the cell line's EBV shows up at all.
EBV=$(awk -F'\t' '$5==3050299{printf "%d", $2; exit}' out.report)
EBV=${EBV:-0}

{
  echo "db_sha256           $DBSHA"
  echo "db_hash_k2d_mb      $HASHMB"
  echo "pairs_processed     $PROC   want exactly 24148993"
  echo "                           == seqkit's per-mate read count (== bwa primary / 2)"
  echo "classified          $CLASS   ($PCT%)   want exactly 21047258"
  echo "unclassified        $UNCL"
  echo "class+unclass       $SUM   want == pairs_processed   [CONSERVATION]"
  echo "human_clade_pairs   $HUMAN   ($HUMANPCT%)   want exactly 20928455"
  echo "ebv_clade_pairs     $EBV   want > 0 (HG00096 is an EBV-transformed cell line)"
  echo "top_species_taxid   $TOPTAX   want 9606 (these are 1000 Genomes human reads)"
  echo "wall_s              $WALL"
  echo "tmpfs_peak_used_mb  $PEAK"
  echo "host_mem_peak_mb    $RSS"
  echo "-- top 3 species by clade reads --"
  printf '%s\n' "$TOPS"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$PROC" = '24148993'
test "$SUM"  = "$PROC"
test "$CLASS" = '21047258'
test "$HUMAN" = '20928455'
test "$TOPTAX" = '9606'
test "$EBV" -gt 0
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
